$comment: Draft from the owner's decision of 2026-10-31: the product-data pack owns the promotion calendar; the kit's single-day list, the Meta pack's decision, the creative pack's offer window and the Google pack's calendar read it. A promotion period follows the calendar's window, not a number said aloud.
title: promo.calendar/1
description: The sale and festival windows of each market, one row per window, written once by the pack that owns the product data so every pack that plans around a promotion reads the same dates.
x-consumers: operators (gads, meta-ads), makers, the kit's single-day list
x-rules: A window belongs to one market; the same festival in two markets is two rows, each with its own dates.
A market with no calendar has no rows: absent, never invented, and a reader treats it as unknown, not as no promotion.
end is the last day of the window, inclusive; end is never before start.
A promotion period follows the window of its row, not a length said aloud.
Dates are the market's own calendar days; produced_at carries its zone.

producer.description: The pack that wrote the document (its CLI word).

produced_at.description: When the document was written: ISO 8601 with its zone.

rows.description: One row per window per market.

market.description: The market the window holds in, as the packs name markets (an ISO 3166 country or region code such as TW or HK).

name.description: The window's name as the market's calendar words it.

start.description: The first day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD, in the market's own calendar.

end.description: The last day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive.

source.description: Where the window came from (the calendar file or the person who gave it), so a reader can ask again.
